To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the short circuit level of the system increases when a PV system is islanded.
the grid-connected inverters are capable to detect and disconnect the system under islanding condition without violating the specified standards.
a grid-connected inverter may contribute to a fault in the event of unintentional islands, which can be modeled using a simple circuit model.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the impact of unintentional islanded distributed generation systems on the short circuit level.
the impact of DG penetration in a distribution system and the need to upgrade the protective devices in a power distribution system.
the impact of the grid-connected PV system on the distribution feeder protection in the event of unintentional grid islanding.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the fault current levels in the event of unintentional grid-connected PV islanding are higher than the fault current levels without PV islanding.
the short circuit levels of the distribution system are affected by the presence of distributed generation and the way it is incorporated in the distribution system.
the grid-connected PV system is not a significant contributor to the short circuit level in an event of a fault.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
, the fault current contribution of the grid-connected PV system is not negligible.
the fault current contribution of the PV grid-connected system is a function of the inverter’s control algorithm and its settings.
the short-circuit level in distribution networks can be increased due to the fault contribution of DG units.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a power flow study can be used to estimate the short circuit level in a distribution system with DG penetration, and the accuracy of such estimation depends on the selected model.
, the short circuit level of the distribution system is not a fixed value, but rather it can be changed depending on the type of distributed generation and its operating mode.
the short circuit levels of a distribution system can be increased by incorporating DG into the system.
